  1. Show HN: Agweb – a browser for agents that stays out of your way

    • AI
    • Web Browsers

    109 points · 37 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 14:08 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Agweb is an open-source macOS browser for coding agents, built on WebKit. It exposes a Playwright-like shell CLI, keeps agent tabs visible in one non-focus-stealing window, and suspends idle tabs.

    Discussion — Interest centered on avoiding agent-browser focus theft, bot detection, shared login sessions, visual feedback, and resource use. The author said it is WebKit-only with no CDP; profile forking is not yet implemented, though saved state can be loaded into a fresh workspace.

  2. Show HN: Zigzag, a native Mac browser for people leaving Arc

    • Web Browsers

    122 points · 74 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 13:17 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Zigzag is a free, Apache-2.0 native macOS browser written in Swift on WebKit, aimed at Arc users. It requires macOS 15.4+, uses a sidebar with spaces and profiles, imports Arc data, supports Chrome Web Store extensions, and advertises no account or telemetry. The README says WebKit is supplied and security-updated by macOS, while the app adds Arc-like organization, split view, Reader, ad blocking, and other features.

    Discussion — Several users reported that it feels responsive and uses less memory than Arc or alternatives; extension compatibility and Arc-like workflow were recurring positives. Others questioned the proliferation and long-term viability of Arc replacements, compared it with Zen/Firefox and Safari, and raised security concerns about a solo, AI-assisted browser project. The author described WebKit process sandboxing, separate helpers for untrusted files, public security advisories, and personal code review/testing.
